races.name: Irish EBF Auction Series Race

runners_data.name: Zoar
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 6f Good trip and finished second in identical conditions — course-and-distance proven form, Donnacha O'Brien yard in fine recent shape (1 from 16 over 14 days but that belies quality), and Paddy Harnett (3lb claimer) keeps the weight down; the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field with a clear route to uncontested lead.
runners_data.comment: Zoar won last time out and was a close second two starts back, arriving here in good heart on a quick 17-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going; he carries 138 lb from stall five, and our figures rank him second of the six.

runners_data.name: Nation Blaze
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides, which is unusual and worth noting; ran 8th and 9th in his two starts with a clear fade pattern, returning after 49 days off and his only Good-ground run produced a below-par effort — the combination of the fade flag and layoff makes it hard to construct a winning scenario here.
runners_data.comment: Nation Blaze has run over today's trip and going, arrives here freshened up after 49 days off, and a trainer striking at 30% over the past fortnight gives him a strong handler angle from stall 4; the risk is his recent form reads eighth and ninth, leaving him yet to score in his last two starts.

runners_data.name: Eyeconic
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan retains the ride for J A Stack but this runner finished 11th on her only start over this exact course and distance on Good ground and is flagged as a fader — the hold-up style is genuine but her sole piece of form provides no platform for optimism unless that run dramatically understated her.
runners_data.comment: Eyeconic arrives winless in recent starts and our figures rank her fifth of six, making her hard to fancy on paper, though she has run over today's trip and going before and a 17-day break at least suggests she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: The Scallionator
runners_data.note: Michael Mulvany's runner has won once and placed twice over 6f on Good ground in six similar appearances, showing solid consistent form at this level; naturally a prominent runner who wants to race forward, he is likely to find himself shuffled back by the congested pace picture, which places him out of his optimal role.
runners_data.comment: Returned a winner four starts back and a close second five starts back, The Scallionator brings strong credentials to this, with experience of both today's trip and going, fresh enough at 31 days since his last run, and he tops the ratings from stall one.

runners_data.name: Fighting Tears
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 6f on Good ground and arrives here in career-best condition for A Oliver, who has had one winner from 17 runners over the past fortnight; like The Scallionator, Fighting Tears wants to race prominently but the field's pace dynamics mean she cannot expect to slot into her natural position unchallenged — her style fit is compromised as a result.
runners_data.comment: Fighting Tears arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a solid profile heading in; at 125 lb from stall 3, the weight could be the one factor to overcome.

runners_data.name: Belle Parvenue
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed on debut for Eddie and Patrick Harty, partnered by the experienced Chris Hayes; the UNKNOWN going flag means we have no evidence base for any assessment — she could be a well-prepared debutant or simply making up numbers, and her OR of 120 is a starting handicap mark rather than a form reading.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement on debut, Belle Parvenue is yet to score but her lightly raced profile leaves plenty to work with; drawing stall six and carrying 120 lb, she is one to watch as she steps into the unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Zoar is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with only six runners and no genuine rival to pressure her from the outset, she is set to control this race from the gates at a sustainable, uncontested tempo over six furlongs on Good ground at Cork. Fighting Tears and The Scallionator are both natural prominent types, but the field is congested with runners wanting that early position — both are mapped to midfield as they are unlikely to secure their preferred ground in this configuration, leaving Zoar to dictate without meaningful interference. Belle Parvenue is a complete unknown on debut, while Nation Blaze and Eyeconic carry fade warnings that undermine their finishing claims. This race shape — an uncontested leader setting a controlled pace — squarely favours the front-running profile and any horse with the tactical speed to track Zoar in the first two; closers will find the pace insufficiently hot to generate a meaningful finishing advantage from off it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Zoar Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Zoar breaks cleanly and immediately establishes control without any rival willing or able to push her through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Zoar sets an unhurried but honest tempo and, with no one forcing the issue, quickens or simply sustains her run into the straight; her Good-ground form profile and O'Brien yard angle make her the natural beneficiary of a front-running shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Collide
scenarios.trigger: If Fighting Tears or The Scallionator challenge Zoar hard from the outset, injecting enough pace to compromise the leader's stamina.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop stretches the field and sets up a race where a horse running prominently but just off the pressure — Fighting Tears if she gets position — arrives with momentum at the furlong pole; the pace-on shape still suits prominent profiles over hold-up types.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the leaders tie each other up, creating a truly run race that enables a hold-up horse to deliver off the bridle.
scenarios.body: Eyeconic is the only natural hold-up type in the field, but her sole run produced an 11th-place finish on this exact track and trip with a fade flag attached, making this scenario heavily dependent on a horse with a weak profile for it; Belle Parvenue on debut is a wildcard but entirely unknown.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Upsets Form
scenarios.trigger: If Belle Parvenue, entirely unexposed on debut, possesses hidden ability and finds a favourable trip through the race.
scenarios.body: A first-time-out runner from Eddie and Patrick Harty with Chris Hayes aboard could be deliberately targeted at this race with a readied youngster; if she shows natural early pace she could land prominently and benefit from any collapse in the principals.

watchPoints.text: Watch Zoar's gate — if she breaks sharply and immediately goes to the front without challenge, the race is likely over as a contest inside the first furlong; any stumble or slow break invites Fighting Tears and The Scallionator to grab the rail and transforms the shape entirely.

Fighting Tears and The Scallionator will both be eyeing the same prominent position from stalls — monitor the first two furlongs for a pace battle between these two natural front-runners that could inflate the tempo beyond what Zoar intended to set.

Nation Blaze returns after 49 days off with a fade flag and uninspiring form figures of 8-9; if he is being freshened for a specific reason (e.g. yard confidence) and breaks prominently, he could complicate the pace map before weakening — watch early market moves.

Belle Parvenue's debut market position at the off will be informative — a well-backed debutant from the Harty yard with Chris Hayes suggests a horse readied to run well, while a drifting SP would suggest she is simply gaining experience.

Eyeconic is the only true hold-up runner but has a single start showing 11th place with a fade; if she is seen to travel with any early comfort and move smoothly through the field in the straight, it would be the most meaningful piece of new information this race generates.

races.name: Coolmore Stud Gleneagles Irish EBF (C & G) Maiden

runners_data.name: Ar Son Na Cuise
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien runner who has shown a hold-up style in both career starts over 7f on Good, recording finishing positions of 10 and 16 — dropping back to 6f and racing in a field loaded with hold-up types means he is unlikely to obtain his natural position, and his fade pattern in both runs offers limited encouragement.

runners_data.name: El Domino
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery takes the ride for his own yard on a colt who has run twice over this exact trip on Good ground, finishing 10th and 6th, giving him more race experience than most rivals; a prominent style is genuinely suited to this pace shape if he can tuck in behind the two front-runners and pick up in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Jungle Wise
runners_data.note: Ben Coen is a strong booking for Daniel James Murphy, whose 11% T14 strike rate is worth noting on a debutant whose going profile is entirely unknown; the complete absence of form data means his chance is opaque, but the jockey-trainer combination and a pace-contested race that could set up a late run are factors to monitor.

runners_data.name: Marco Polo
runners_data.note: A P O'Brien colt who placed second over 6f on Good and carries confirmed front-running style into a race where he meets another genuine leader in Revelator — Wayne Lordan will need to judge whether to press or sit just off, as matching Revelator throughout risks emptying both horses before the line.

runners_data.name: Moon Sand
runners_data.note: Joseph Patrick O'Brien's hold-up type has finished ninth in both career starts over further trips on Good ground, showing a clear fade tendency; stepping back to 6f against livelier pace does nothing obvious to cure the lack of finish, and Scott McCullagh inherits a difficult task from the rear.

runners_data.name: Revelator
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner has 60 days between runs, which can sharpen or blunt a 2-year-old's readiness, and his form reads 7th then 3rd over this exact 6f on Good — Josh Halley's yard fires at just 20% T14, so the homework is done but the margins are fine; if Andrew Slattery can get him out cleanly and at his own rhythm, he sets the race up for himself or the prominent types behind him.

runners_data.name: Snapequus
runners_data.note: Another Joseph Patrick O'Brien hold-up runner with two starts at 7f on Good, both finishing 11th, with Declan McDonogh now booked; the drop to 6f and a fast early pace do not obviously help a horse that fades consistently, and three O'Brien hold-up types in the same race suggests one may be a pacemaker or market mover rather than a primary betting vehicle.

runners_data.name: Tennesspeed
runners_data.note: Mrs John Harrington's runner hasn't raced for 98 days after finishing 11th over 6f on Good last time, which is a significant layoff for a 2-year-old stepping back into maiden company; Shane Foley is a reliable booking but the fade on debut and the long absence leave plenty to prove before trusting a hold-up profile in a pace-contested race.

runners_data.name: Timucua Gold
runners_data.note: Colin Keane's mount for Noel Meade was beaten around 8 lengths finishing 8th over 7f on Good, showing a fade pattern on debut, and now drops to 6f with a style listed as unknown/hold-up; the Keane booking gives it credibility, but a lightly-raced horse stepping into a pace-pressed race needs to show a gear change that debut footage did not confirm.

races.paceDynamic: Revelator and Marco Polo are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the gates, creating a genuinely competitive early pace over 6f on Good ground at Cork — neither is a natural settler, so the gallop should be honest rather than manufactured. The duel between these two means the fractions will be set by ambition rather than tactics, compressing the field early and likely burning off runners who try to match them. With multiple hold-up types (Moon Sand, Snapequus, Tennesspeed, Ar Son Na Cuise) all carrying weak form figures and fade patterns, and the pace fight serving as a natural filter, prominent-to-midfield types who can settle just off the speed and pick up through the final two furlongs are best placed to capitalise. The field holds more hold-up horses than can genuinely operate from the rear in a race this hot early — Ar Son Na Cuise is a natural hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map, but El Domino and Marco Polo are better positioned to control their own destiny in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Two Burn, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Revelator and Marco Polo fight for the lead and set an honest-to-strong pace that softens both, a well-positioned prominent or early-midfield runner sweeps past the tiring duo inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: El Domino has twice run on good ground over this trip and holds a prominent style that allows him to track the pace without chasing it, giving him an ideal launching platform; Marco Polo could still find enough to pick up if he settles fractionally behind Revelator rather than matching him stride for stride.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Revelator secures the lead unchallenged and Marco Polo fails to press him hard early, a controlled front-runner can dictate terms and quicken clear off a moderate pace.
scenarios.body: Revelator has placed over 6f on Good ground and with an uncontested lead on a flat track he could simply control the fractions and conserve enough for a late surge; this scenario rewards the horse that gets to the front cleanest in the first furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace duel between Revelator and Marco Polo is genuinely fierce and both capitulate inside the final furlong, a hold-up runner with a turn of foot could collect.
scenarios.body: Timucua Gold and Tennesspeed sit furthest back but both have conspicuous fade patterns in their histories, making a late sustained run unlikely; this scenario is possible only if the pace genuinely collapses and a horse finds a clear run from off the pace in the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debut/Lightly Raced Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If Jungle Wise or Timucua Gold have been schooled specifically for this shorter trip and arrive significantly more forward than their lightly-raced profiles suggest, an unknown quantity wins on raw ability.
scenarios.body: Jungle Wise is completely unexposed with an unknown going profile and Ben Coen in the saddle is a meaningful booking for a yard that fires at 11%; a maiden with contested pace and moderate rivals is the type of race a well-bred debutant can exploit if the ability is there.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Marco Polo or Revelator actually cedes the lead in the first furlong — if both refuse to settle, the early tempo will be fierce and both risk weakening sharply inside the final 2f, opening the door for El Domino to sweep past.

Jungle Wise is an unexposed debutant with a strong jockey booking in Ben Coen; horses with no public form can arrive completely ready in a race like this, so monitor market moves in the final minutes before the off.

Joseph Patrick O'Brien saddles three hold-up types (Moon Sand, Snapequus, Ar Son Na Cuise) in the same field — watch which, if any, drifts in the market, as multiple runners from the same yard in a maiden often indicates a stable pecking order that the odds will reflect.

Revelator's 60-day break is the longest layoff in the field and warrants monitoring — a 2-year-old returning from two months off to lead a contested pace needs to be spot-on, and any signs of freshness or greenness in the parade ring are meaningful.

El Domino is the only runner combining Good-ground 6f experience, a prominent style genuinely suited to today's pace shape, and a yards that fires at a healthy 7/23 T14 — if the market shortens him in the final show, the convergence of factors is worth noting.

races.name: Follow Us On Instagram Handicap

runners_data.name: Sommelier
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse for Kieran Cotter, off 43 days and carrying the flag for a trainer in poor 14-day form (0/2); the fade-in-finish flag is a significant concern in a race likely to be run at maximum pace, and 15th of 15 in similar going last time is hard to overcome.
runners_data.comment: Sommelier has run over today's trip and going before, and his win four starts back shows he can produce on the right day; at 140 lb from stall 8, the burden he carries is the factor rivals will be hoping tells against him.

runners_data.name: Go Athletico
runners_data.note: Adrian McGuinness yard in solid 14-day form (4/30) and this eight-year-old veteran is a genuine hold-up type on good ground with 10 career placings in similar conditions; runs best when getting a clear late passage and the strong pace here sets up his style perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Placed second three starts back and again five starts back, Go Athletico arrives here 18 days fresh with experience of today's trip and going; winless in his last six starts is the reservation, but top-rated among 25 runners and carrying 139 lb from stall 25, he looks the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Real Encounter
runners_data.note: Shane Foley takes the ride for Mrs Harrington and this lightly-framed three-year-old showed real ability when placed at 2f and 5f on good; stepping up to 6f after a 53-day break, natural prominent runner who will need clean passage early in a field of 25.
runners_data.comment: Real Encounter shaped with plenty of promise when third two starts back and second three starts back, and has run over today's trip and going, giving her a solid fitness foundation returning after 53 days; the unplaced effort last time is the one note of caution.

runners_data.name: Tokyo Treasure
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who has been campaigning at 7-8f and is sharply dropping back in trip to 6f; good ground record is solid (7/7) but the step down in distance is the big unknown, and the trainer has had no 14-day form to speak of.
runners_data.comment: Tokyo Treasure shaped with some promise when second three starts back, but he is winless in his last five starts and a 136 lb burden from stall 19 makes life harder still; experience over today's trip and going offers some encouragement, though he has plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Fox In Flight
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for David Marnane who showed a placed effort at 5f on good; the form figures over 6f on good are uninspiring, but at 3 years old with conditions in the OK bracket there is latent improvement if traffic allows a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Fox In Flight faces a stiff ask off 135 lb from stall six, and his recent form — unplaced last time out and two nines in there — offers little encouragement, though he has run over today's distance and going before and is fit enough at 25 days.

runners_data.name: Whiskey And Beer
runners_data.note: Back after a staggering 760 days off the track and has a fade-in-finish flag attached; even with a reasonable course profile in three career runs, the extreme layoff in a 25-runner sprint makes this a significant risk proposition.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and returning from a 760-day absence, Whiskey And Beer faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and carries 135 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Jon Riggens
runners_data.note: Edward Lynam's eight-year-old is a proper hold-up horse who won over course and distance last time at 6f on good; the 94-day break is the concern, but Ben Coen takes over and the tongue-tie and visor combo suggests the yard is set to produce a sharp performance.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but that victory came 94 days ago, leaving fitness a question mark, and he has experience of today's distance and going; carrying 134 lb from stall 24, his inconsistent recent record — seventh, sixth, seventh and unplaced before that win — tempers enthusiasm.

runners_data.name: Tornado Kiss
runners_data.note: Trainer/jockey combination in Andrew Slattery has clocked 7/23 in 14-day form which is a bright angle; off 98 days and dropping to 6f from 5f sprint form, this three-year-old prominent type won over 5f on good and the extra furlong is unproven.
runners_data.comment: Tornado Kiss boasts a win in her last five starts and has run over today's trip and going, while a trainer hitting 30% over the past fortnight adds serious confidence; the concern is a return from 98 days off, with her recent efforts trending the wrong way.

runners_data.name: Mehman
runners_data.note: P.J.F. Murphy's seven-year-old is in truth a hold-up horse whose natural position is at the rear — the blinkers flag is noted — but with more true closers than the field can accommodate at the back, it will likely be closer to midfield than its natural style; sim-going figures (3/15) are a concern at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Mehman is yet to find his best form in recent runs, though a second and a third do feature deeper in that sequence; he has experience of today's trip and going and returns after 22 days, but 133 lb from stall 12 makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Shadow Of The Moon
runners_data.note: Hold-up type for a trainer with some 14-day form (1/4) and a fade-in-finish flag that is hard to ignore over a sharp 6f; won over 5f on good and the extra furlong plus 73 days off could blunt the finishing effort.
runners_data.comment: Shadow Of The Moon showed she can win in recent starts, with a second two starts back a further positive, but has been unplaced on her last outing and returns after 73 days off; she has run over today's distance and going before and carries 133 lb from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Cry
runners_data.note: Terry Casey (7lb claimer) partners this lightly-raced three-year-old who has a solid win over 5f on good in the book; 6f is one furlong further than the winning trip and the hold-up style means the large field is a real traffic hazard — nine runs without a top-six finish over this trip tells a story.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Cry returns just seven days after his last outing, which may raise freshness concerns, and his recent string of ninths makes it hard to fancy him confidently, though a win five starts back and a fourth three starts back hint at residual ability over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Dawn Romance
runners_data.note: Colin Keane is the significant jockey booking for M.D. O'Callaghan's three-year-old who won over 6f on good and has the prominent style to sit just off the pace; off 62 days, the yard has been in recent form (4/15) and Keane will ensure a good position without overexposing early.
runners_data.comment: Dawn Romance showed she can win in recent starts, but four subsequent efforts have been largely disappointing, and 62 days off adds a fitness query; she has run over today's trip and going, and carries 132 lb from stall 16.

runners_data.name: Gerrit's Gem
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for J.G. Coogan who has placed on good ground in the past but recent figures (three non-completions and a 10th) make current form hard to assess; the 11-day turnaround is quick and Jack Cleary's 5lb claim helps on weight but not on form.
runners_data.comment: Gerrit's Gem showed a flash of form with a third last time out after a lean spell, and he has run over today's distance and going before, though winless in his last five starts he faces stiff competition carrying 132 lb from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Leveraging
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Sheila Lavery who drops back to 6f on good having won over this trip before; the 37-day break and modest trainer 14-day stats (1/8) are tempered by the fact that this horse will lead — its chance depends entirely on whether the pace war with Grande Cuvee and Venetian Star leaves it with anything in reserve.
runners_data.comment: Leveraging has won in recent starts but that solitary success is sandwiched by a string of disappointing efforts, and he ranks 19th of 25 on our figures, making him hard to fancy; the experience over today's trip and going, plus stall one, are the only crumbs of comfort.

runners_data.name: Grande Cuvee
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan's mount for J.A. Stack is a confirmed front-runner who has finished placed twice on good ground this year; the 10-day turnaround is quick and positive, and Heffernan's ability to dictate a comfortable gallop is the key to whether this horse can see out the 6f in front.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked well down our figures, Grande Cuvee faces a stiff ask here, though she has shown consistency with two seconds and a third in recent starts and has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Soulful Diva
runners_data.note: David Marnane's three-year-old is a hold-up type with a placed run over 5f on good; Nathan Crosse rides and the horse has been busy (18 days since last run) which can suit, but finishing ninth last time out on the same course and distance is not encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts but Soulful Diva brings distance and going experience to the table, and a rating of 77 suggests she retains ability; the unplaced effort eighteen days ago is a concern, though second two starts back hints she can get competitive.

runners_data.name: All The Girls
runners_data.note: James Ryan partners this prominent-style three-year-old who placed over 6f on soft and has some form on fast-ish ground; the trainer has had 1/16 in 14 days which is moderate and with a field of 25 prominent types she is likely to find herself shuffled further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in her last six starts, All The Girls does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and her placed efforts — second last time out and third three starts back — show she can threaten; 130 lb from stall 22 are the checks on her claims.

runners_data.name: My Cubby Bear
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's three-year-old returns after 299 days off and has only three career runs in the book, all on artificial or easy ground; W.J. Lee takes the ride but the lengthy absence and unproven good-ground form make this a significant unknown in a competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and last seen on a racecourse 299 days ago, My Cubby Bear faces a stiff task ranked last on our figures, though she has run over today's trip before and her second two starts back offers a rare glimmer of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Send Harry
runners_data.note: Jimmy Dalton's 7lb claim helps on weight for this prominent-style four-year-old whose best form has come at 7f on good; the step down to 6f and a history of being placed (12/15 placings in sim going!) rather than winning raises the familiar bridesmaid concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 20th of 25 on our figures, Send Harry faces a stiff task from stall 17 carrying 130 lb, though he has run over today's trip and going before and the fourth three starts back offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Cashel Blue
runners_data.note: K.J. Condon's three-year-old is genuinely a hold-up horse with two wins on good ground over 5f and a place over this trip — but there are more true closers than the rear of the field can hold, meaning it will likely track closer to midfield than it wants; the 7lb claimer Reese Holohan navigates the largest field of its career so far.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our assessments, Cashel Blue makes it hard to build a case despite winning last time out, as her overall recent profile — unplaced and fifth in the two starts before that — reflects the inconsistency; she has run over today's trip and going, and a quick turnaround at least confirms she is fit.

runners_data.name: Venetian Star
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner for Patrick Foley who ran 2nd over 7f on soft last year; the 8-day turnaround is quick and Ronan Whelan picks up the ride, but seven-length-plus defeats at 7-8f on good suggest the front-running tactics at a shorter trip is a last-resort move rather than natural class.
runners_data.comment: Venetian Star is winless in his last six starts, though a second four starts back and a third six starts back hint at some ability, and he arrives here fresh after just eight days, with experience of both today's trip and conditions; 128 lb from stall two is the burden he must shoulder.

runners_data.name: Nouvel Espoir
runners_data.note: James Barcoe's six-year-old is a true hold-up type who has placed repeatedly on good ground over 5-6f — yet the field is saturated with closers, and in a 25-runner sprint the wide draw and crowded rear positions will present real challenges; the 7lb claimer on board amplifies the navigational difficulty.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of the field on our figures, Nouvel Espoir has been placed just once in his last six starts, though that third last time out at least hints at a flicker of form, and he has experience of today's trip and going, carrying 126 lb from stall 18.

runners_data.name: Pinar Del Rio
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh takes the ride for Alan McIntyre on this seven-year-old prominent type who has four placings in sim-going conditions out of 15; the horse has been off 18 days and drops slightly in class, but the form string (9-4057) shows nothing better than fourth recently.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 21 of 25 on our figures, Pinar Del Rio makes a tough case, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns fit enough on an 18-day break, carrying 125 lb from stall 20.

runners_data.name: The Bear Trap
runners_data.note: 492 days off the track is an extreme layoff for a five-year-old prominent runner; Adrian McGuinness yard in form (4/30) is a genuine angle but the visor first-time-up and the lengthy absence in a 25-runner sprint suggests this is a fitness-building run rather than a realistic winner.
runners_data.comment: The Bear Trap won three starts back but has been unplaced last time out and returns after a lengthy 492-day absence, which is the obvious query; he has run over today's trip and going before, and a rating of 74 offers some encouragement from stall 23 off 123 lb.

runners_data.name: Coincidental Glory
runners_data.note: McGuinness's third runner in the race and in truth a prominent horse who gets bumped back to a midfield position by the sheer weight of
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 18th of 25 on our figures, Coincidental Glory looks firmly up against it here, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick turnaround just 11 days since his last outing.

races.paceDynamic: Leveraging, Grande Cuvee, and Venetian Star are all confirmed front-runners in a 25-runner field, and with 10 of 25 wanting prominent positions, the early scramble for the rail and front rank will be fierce — a strong, unrelenting gallop from the outset is almost certain. The three leaders will press each other through the first two furlongs, compressing the pace and creating a wall of horses that makes clean passage through the field extremely difficult 2-3 out, particularly for those starting in double-figures stalls. This race shape — a genuinely contested, high-tempo 6f on good ground — classically burns out the pace setters and sets the race up for horses who can travel smoothly in mid-division and produce a sustained run from the 2f pole rather than a sharp sprint. The field holds more prominent types than can realistically hold that position: Coincidental Glory, Real Encounter, All The Girls, and Send Harry are the ones most likely to jostle for the front-rank spots, with several inevitably sliding back through the field under pressure in the early stages. The clear tactical verdict is that the race shape strongly favours genuine, relaxed midfield closers who switch off behind the pace and finish strongly, with hold-up horses having a fighting chance only if they can find clear running down the outside from 2f out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Feast
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners fight each other through a truly brutal early gallop and burn out inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Leveraging, Grande Cuvee, and Venetian Star set a scorching tempo that drags the prominent pack along with them, leaving the field ragged and tiring entering the final 2f; genuine midfield horses who have settled and conserved energy sweep past the fading leaders in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fierce but one prominent horse settles just behind the leaders, avoids the worst of the scrimmage, and picks off the tiring front-runners.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting fourth or fifth, close enough to the speed to avoid traffic but shielded from the full force of the early duel, finds the most economical route and has enough left to sustain a run through the final furlong; this profile is best served by a horse with tactical speed and a recent sharp prep.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the confirmed leaders — most likely Grande Cuvee or Leveraging — breaks cleanly, establishes an uncontested lead before the pace heats up, and controls the gallop from the front.
scenarios.body: With a large field creating early chaos behind them, a leader who gets a soft lead through the first furlong can control the tempo and coast into the straight with something in reserve; on good ground over 6f at Cork this is more achievable if rivals bump and check each other out of contention early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so strong that even the midfield gets dragged along, and true hold-up horses who sit last early find the widest part of the track and run on fastest of all.
scenarios.body: Note that several horses tagged as hold-up types in this race — Mehman, Cashel Blue, and Nouvel Espoir — are redistributed runners unlikely to get to the rear naturally, which limits the likelihood of this shape genuinely playing out; a true late flourish requires those horses to race entirely against their likely actual early positioning.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies Maiden
Follow Us On X Handicap

runners_data.name: Green Kite
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a tendency to fade in the finish; Colin Keane adds significant class, but 63 days off and a flat record of 0W0P on similar good ground over 7f makes this a tough ask in a 25-runner field where getting a clear run from the rear is a serious concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Green Kite nonetheless shaped with clear promise when a close second two runs back, and his experience over today's trip and going underlines his claims as a leading threat; the 63-day absence is the one factor to weigh.

runners_data.name: Spent All Me Money
runners_data.note: Runs in a hood and genuinely stays further than today's trip, with a decent 2W4P record on similar ground; a true hold-up operator who will be stuck deep in traffic in this field, and the step back to 7f from 8f is unlikely to help getting into the race early enough.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and carrying the top weight of 140 lb from stall 12, Spent All Me Money arrives with experience of today's distance and going and our ratings rank him top of these, making him the one to beat despite being winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Battleforsupremacy
runners_data.note: Ben Coen takes the ride on this hold-up type who produced a 3rd at Naas last time over 7f on standard ground; lacks similar-going form here (0W0P in 3 attempts on good), but the trainer has had a winner in the past fortnight and the horse's best runs have come over this trip.
runners_data.comment: Battleforsupremacy shaped with promise when third two starts back and brings distance and going experience to the table, while his speed rating of 61 underlines his threat from stall seven carrying 136 lb — the concern is his unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Lilbittyprettyone
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer with a pronounced finishing fade who has been running consistently over 5f and 8f rather than today's 7f; the trip looks an awkward middle-ground for this horse, and two runs at 9+ in this grade on good ground suggest it will struggle to pick up cleanly from off the pace in a large field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Lilbittyprettyone has experience of today's trip and going, yet a string of mid-to-rear finishes makes improvement a necessity, and carrying 136 lb from stall six does little to ease the task.

runners_data.name: Princess Chloe
runners_data.note: Siobhan Rutledge takes the ride on a hold-up type with a solid recent record — a 4th, 5th, and 2nd in her last three on good ground over 6-7f; the sim-going figures of 3/7 (0W1P) are modest, but the 7f trip here suits and she has finished in the first five in five of her last six.
runners_data.comment: Placed two starts back on the same distance and going, Princess Chloe arrives here with sound course-and-going experience and our rating has her fourth of 25 — yet to land a race in recent starts is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Frosted Sky
runners_data.note: Consistently finishing in the rear third on good ground (0W0P in 3 similar-going runs), this McLoughlin-trained filly also carries a fade flag and steps back up to 7f having been beaten off over 5-6f; not obviously placed to reverse that trend from a deep hold-up position.
runners_data.comment: Frosted Sky has run over today's trip and going before, but winless in her last four starts and ranked tenth of twenty-five here, her recent string of unplaced efforts makes improvement essential, though 37 days off may have freshened her up.

runners_data.name: Cisterna
runners_data.note: Trainer-jockey combination (Andrew Slattery, self-trained) has been in excellent form — 7/23 over 14 days — and this 3yo has a genuine winning effort on the board; steps up from 8f to 7f which is a shortening of trip, but good-ground form is strong (11/15 runners, 1W2P) and has been kept busy with only 9 days since last run.
runners_data.comment: Cisterna won one start back from six in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going, but unplaced last time and carrying 133 lb from stall 10 tempers enthusiasm; the trainer's sharp 30% strike rate over 14 days offers the main reason for optimism.

runners_data.name: Gilts
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground at this sort of level and has a place in that trip-going combination; the fade flag is a concern, but Jack Cleary's 5lb claim helps offset the weight and the horse has more pace form at 7f than many in this field.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win one start back but has shown inconsistency around it, and her figures suggest she runs just below the level needed here; she has experience of today's trip and conditions, though 132 lb from stall 20 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Lust
runners_data.note: An 8yo who is a genuine deep hold-up type — mapped to midfield here because the field holds more closers than the map can place — meaning it will likely race even further out of role than shown; best form has come over 8-10f, not today's 7f, and the STYLE_FIT discount of 0.92 is relevant.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Lust does hold a fitness edge at just eight days since his last run and has experience of today's distance and going, though third three starts back is the only crumb of encouragement in a largely disappointing recent sequence, and 132 lb from stall 17 adds to the challenge.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Rory Mulligan (5lb claim) rides a prominent-style horse with a strong record on good ground — 13 qualifying runs, 0W6P — who genuinely races prominently and is not redistributed; the 7f trip is shorter than some recent starts but the horse's record at 5-8f on good is consistently competitive.
runners_data.comment: Whatswrongnow has shown consistency without converting, with a third last time out and a second the start before, yet he remains yet to win in his last six starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, but 130 lb from stall 23 makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Seamie Heffernan takes a naturally held-up horse whose true position is further back than the midfield slot shown — the field density pushed it forward on the map; the horse has a win on good ground over 8f and goes well fresh (7d since last run), but the 7f trip is short of its best and the style mismatch is real.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced in three of his last five starts and ranked 19th of 25 on our figures, Micasso is hard to fancy at the weights, though he did win in recent starts and has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Notforalongtime
runners_data.note: A 9yo veteran with hold-up tendencies and a genuine 3rd at 7f on good last time; the field's volume has shifted it to midfield on the map but its real position will be towards the rear, making a clean run in a 25-runner field difficult — though Robbie Colgan is an experienced handler of busy races.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and unplaced on his most recent outing 55 days ago, Notforalongtime does at least have experience over today's trip and conditions, and a rating of 52 offers a sliver of encouragement, though he faces a stiff task from 11th in a field of 25.

runners_data.name: Heart Of Eternity
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's 4yo carries a fade flag and has been placed in the last six days; the horse is a true hold-up type racing effectively out of role — best efforts have come over 5-6f on heavy, and today's good ground over 7f represents a double query on trip and surface sharpness.
runners_data.comment: Heart Of Eternity has run over today's trip and going before, but she arrives winless in her last six starts with a trainer in a difficult patch of form, and her official rating of 46 offers little encouragement from stall 16 carrying 128 lb.

runners_data.name: Linger For Longer
runners_data.note: W J Lee partners this 7yo who has been off 91 days — the longest break in the field — and is a genuine hold-up horse whose map position understates how far back it will likely race; one win on 7f good ground in the recent hist does offer some hope if fit enough.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and 91 days absent, Linger For Longer faces questions about fitness, though she has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 56 offers some encouragement from stall 24 at 127 lb.

runners_data.name: Sayonara
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's in-form stable sends this 3yo out just 10 days after its last run; races prominently and has a useful 6/10 sim-going record including two places at 7-8f on good — the 7f trip is a suitable distance and the horse is not redistributed, meaning it should get closer to its natural racing position than most rivals.
runners_data.comment: Sayonara has been finding his level of late, finishing third last time out and second the start before, yet he remains winless in recent starts and a stall-21 draw adds an unknown element; however, a 10-day turnaround with a trainer firing at 30% gives connections solid grounds for optimism.

runners_data.name: Liamo
runners_data.note: A prominent-style horse (hood and tongue-strap) who won over 7f on good ground last time out at this trip; 46 days since last run may have freshened, and the 3lb claimer Paddy Harnett reduces the burden, though the sim-going record (9/15, 1W3P) suggests the horse is competitive without being dominant.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pair of sixths and a fifth among recent efforts, Liamo is hard to fancy from stall 13 carrying 126 lb, though the runner-up finish last time out offers a slender crumb of comfort and he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Cannonball Queen
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes rides a hold-up type with a finishing-fade flag who has been placed at 7f on good most recently (4th, 6th in last two over this trip); the style mismatch is material given the field size, but the horse does at least have relevant distance form that sets it apart from some redistributed rivals.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked near the foot of our figures, Cannonball Queen faces a stiff ask from stall 25 carrying 125 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a sharp turnaround of just seven days.

runners_data.name: Pick A Window
runners_data.note: Luke McAteer rides this hold-up mare with a fade tendency; the horse's real position is at the rear of the field — the 17th and 12th positions in recent good-ground starts illustrate the challenge — and the 5th over 7f good in the hist is the best evidence of any ability at today's conditions, but it is a long way from a winning profile.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked well down the field on our figures, Pick A Window has little recent form to work with, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after 49 days off.

runners_data.name: She's On The Ball
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan takes the ride on a hold-up type who ran 3rd over 6f on good last time and wears a tongue-strap; the true running position will be deeper than the midfield slot shown, but the horse has a recent placed effort and Lordan's booking is noteworthy — one to respect lightly despite the style compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked twentieth of twenty-five on our figures, She's On The Ball faces a stiff task here, though a third last time out and experience over today's distance and going offer slim crumbs of comfort after 35 days off.

runners_data.name: Lady Landhort
runners_data.note: McLoughlin's third runner in this race; a hold-up type with a fade tendency who has been well beaten in five of six recent starts on good ground, with form figures of 0 in the last three — the redistribution to midfield only papers over a horse that needs significant improvement to feature.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 21 of 25 on our figures, Lady Landhort is hard to fancy despite returning on a reasonable 18-day break; she has run over today's distance and going before, and stall two is noted, but her recent string of unplaced efforts makes her a difficult proposition.

runners_data.name: Niobite
runners_data.note: A 3yo filly who has been recording figures of 6th, 14th, 15th, 12th, 17th in recent starts — all on good ground — and wears a tongue-strap; the fact that her best recent effort was a 6th over 5f does not inspire confidence at 7f in a 25-runner field, and the STYLE_FIT discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Niobite is hard to fancy here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a reasonable 17-day break.

runners_data.name: Tariff
runners_data.note: Maxwell's second runner (alongside Lust), a 3yo hold-up type with a fade flag who has not finished in the first eight in any of its last five starts; the best sim-going effort was a 9th at 7f on good, and the redistribution to midfield does nothing to disguise a horse without the form to win this.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with finishes no better than eighth in recent efforts, Tariff is hard to fancy on these figures, ranked near the foot of the field; has run over today's trip and going, and seven days since his last run at least puts freshness on his side.

runners_data.name: Strikepoint
runners_data.note: No jockey listed — a flag in itself; a natural hold-up type pushed to midfield on the map and carrying a STYLE_FIT discount of 0.90, with best form of a 7th over 6f on good and nothing in the record to suggest a major run from this position in this grade.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Strikepoint nonetheless has experience over today's trip and going to draw on, and an 11-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh; the 126 lb burden from stall 15 are the chief anchors on his chances.

runners_data.name: Haroussa
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, trained by J P Murtagh with 2/25 recent form; carries a fade flag and has been beaten off in all three starts on good ground, but the uncontested lead is a significant tactical advantage — the STYLE_FIT caveat (0.92) relates to its ability
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked 16 of 25 on our assessment, Haroussa faces an uphill task, though she has run over today's trip and going before and returns on a quick ten-day turnaround carrying 137 lb from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Sceitimini
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Sceitimini at least returns on a quick turnaround of ten days and has run over today's distance and going before, though a fifth being his best recent effort and a ranking of twelfth of twenty-five leave him with plenty to find.

races.paceDynamic: Haroussa is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 25-runner field and, critically, appears likely to control proceedings without serious sustained pressure from genuine rivals — the pace map identifies Lust, Strikepoint, Sceitimini, and several others as natural prominent or hold-up types who are unlikely to secure those positions given the size and composition of the field. With Haroussa setting a sustainable, uncontested gallop on good ground over 7f at Cork, this is a tempo that will not burn off the field early but will reward those able to travel close to the pace and produce a measured, controlled finish. The field is dominated by hold-up horses, and with so many true closers unable to race from their preferred position, there will be significant traffic and positional compromises in the rear half. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently — sitting just off Haroussa or in the first half-dozen — over genuine hold-up horses who will be disadvantaged by a field this large at a pace this manageable.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Haroussa dictates an uncontested, sustainable gallop and the field strings out, rewarding horses who track the pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Haroussa sets a comfortable tempo unchallenged from the front, allowing the prominent and pace-tracking horses to travel well within themselves before asserting in the final 2f; with hold-up horses stuck in traffic and unable to build momentum, the winner will most likely emerge from the first six at halfway.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Haroussa goes too fast early or the large field causes interference and bunching, creating a truly run race that sets up a late run.
scenarios.body: A genuine end-to-end gallop — more likely triggered by early jostling in a 25-runner field than by any rival pressing Haroussa — would stretch the field and open a closing lane for the freshest finishers; however, most nominal closers in this race are redistributed and racing out of role, limiting how many true hold-up horses can genuinely benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Chaos, Midfield Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the large field bunches through the first half and a gap opens for a midfield horse who finds clear running early in the straight.
scenarios.body: With 25 runners on a flat 7f track, significant crowding in mid-race is probable, and a horse sitting handy in a genuine midfield position who avoids trouble could thread through while the hold-up horses remain blocked; Whatswrongnow and Sayonara have the form and style to capitalise if they land a clean run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so modest that Haroussa simply idles into the final furlong and the field fails to close.
scenarios.body: Haroussa, despite fading tendencies flagged in form, could benefit from such an unusually calm run through the race that no challenger gets organised in time; this remains the least likely outcome given the size of the field and the pressure that naturally builds in the final 2f of a 25-runner handicap.

races.name: Follow Us On Social Media Maiden
Racing Again September 29th Handicap

runners_data.name: Highbury See See
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for Andrew Slattery, ran 9 days ago and has eight course runs at this trip on good ground — sim-going record of 8 from 15 suggests competence but limited upside off OR 69; Sam Coen (5) on board.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with a third two runs before last offering the sole bright spot in a patchy recent spell, Highbury See See does get today's trip and going, and a trainer firing at 30% over the past fortnight keeps connections hopeful, though his latest ninth is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Autumn Twist
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan runner who won over 17f on good ground last time — the drop to a flat mile is a significant trip concern, but the prominent style and strong sim-going record (3W from 12 on good) gives J M Sheridan a live chance if the pace collapses in front.|
runners_data.comment: Autumn Twist has run over today's trip and going, and his rating of 73 ranks him third of 21 runners, giving him solid claims despite being yet to win in his last five starts — a trainer in the depths of a 0/23 run is the significant concern.

runners_data.name: Blues Emperor
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type dropping back to 8f having run 7f recently; tongue-tie fitted, 49 days off, and trainer William Harvey's 14-day record is a modest 1 from 3 — form figures of 040607 suggest he needs things to fall right.|
runners_data.comment: Blues Emperor arrives here winless in his last six starts, yet our rating of 78 puts him clear at the head of this 21-runner field, and he has run over today's trip and going before, making him the one to beat from stall nine off 139 lb.

runners_data.name: Comfort Line
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran hold-up horse who won over this exact trip on good ground in the form string and carries the visor; Cillian Rowan (10) is in the saddle and Adrian McGuinness's yard is in solid recent form at 4 from 30 over 14 days.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked 15 of 21 on our figures and carrying a hefty 137 lb from stall 15, Comfort Line is hard to fancy despite a third last time out and a win two starts back; he has run over today's trip and going before, but the weight and rating angle make him tough to recommend.

runners_data.name: Greek Flower
runners_data.note: True hold-up type for John Feane who has been off 89 days — that lengthy absence is a concern, and the sim-going figures of 0W 1P from 11 runs on good turf suggest this horse rarely fires to its maximum.|
runners_data.comment: Rated a clear second of 21 in this field, Greek Flower brings solid credentials on distance and going, and her 78 rating puts her among the leading threats here; the worry is she is winless in her last five starts and returns after 89 days off.

runners_data.name: Star Strewn
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for C W J Farrell, won over 7f at Sligo and steps up to a competitive 1m handicap — sim-going record on good is a thin 0W 0P from just 2 runs, and the tongue-tie is retained; Rory Cleary will be pushing forward from the outset.|
runners_data.comment: Star Strewn won four starts back and has run over today's trip and going, with a speed rating of 76 lending substance to her claims from stall four; the concern is her last three runs have all been disappointing, and she needs to rediscover that earlier form.

runners_data.name: Storm Averted
runners_data.note: Maurice Ahern's five-year-old is a natural hold-up horse wearing the tongue-tie, but the crowded 21-runner field means Adam Browne-Souza (7) will struggle to find the rear position this horse needs — style fit of 0.92 reflects that compromise.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and unplaced most recently, Storm Averted at least has experience of today's trip and conditions, though her record suggests she'll need to find plenty from stall six off 136 lb to make a significant impression.

runners_data.name: Elusive Duke
runners_data.note: Colin Keane takes the ride on this lightly raced four-year-old who has placed five times from 15 good-ground starts (1W) — genuinely a horse who wants to come from off the pace, but the field size means he'll likely race closer than ideal, tempering confidence in his finish.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 18th of 21 on our figures, Elusive Duke faces a stiff task from stall 17 carrying 134 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and posted three seconds in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Trumph
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's three-year-old is flagged as fading in the finish and the recent form of 8-060 is weak; hold-up style in a 21-runner field with two front-runners blazing means Shane Foley will need significant luck in running.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Trumph faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a quick turnaround of just 13 days.

runners_data.name: Coasting
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for David Marnane who hasn't run in 117 days — just three career runs to go on (form: 459) and the combination of a long layoff and a tough 21-runner handicap makes this a speculative entry.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and returning after a 117-day absence, Coasting has experience over today's trip and going to call on, though a ninth last time out and a rating of 67 leave him with plenty to find from stall 10 off 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Holy Lettuce
runners_data.note: Unclassified style (U) for K J Condon, ran eight days ago and has four consecutive runs on good ground — the 2nd placed run at 8f on good is encouraging and W J Lee is a strong booking; watched carefully as a tactical wildcard.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 16 of 21 on our figures, Holy Lettuce faces a stiff ask here; a second three starts back offers a crumb of hope, but a seventh last time out and 133 lb to carry make him hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Navajo Point
runners_data.note: Has a win and a place from nine good-ground runs and finished 1st and 2nd recently, but is flagged for fading in the finish and is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into midfield by the large field — style fit of 0.92 means Paddy Harnett (3) faces a positioning challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Navajo Point has winning form from last time out and returns fit on just eight days' rest, with experience of both today's trip and going in his favour, but carrying 133 lb from stall 14 and ranked nineteenth of twenty-one on our figures, he looks hard to fancy at this level.

runners_data.name: Sherekiya
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's unclassified three-year-old has a 3rd place from five good-ground runs and is ridden by Chris Hayes — 24 days since last run, and the unknown tactical profile makes this a horse to observe rather than rely upon in a complex race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Sherekiya nonetheless showed a return to form with a third last time out, and has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 133 lb from stall 12, she gives each-way hope despite ranking mid-division on our figures.

runners_data.name: Go Out
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner for Daniel Murphy who has course-form at this trip — form figures of 769034 are modest but the style suits a pace-collapsed scenario; Terry Casey (7) will look to slot in prominently behind the front-running battle.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Go Out does bring distance and going experience to the table, and a recent third two starts back suggests he retains some ability; however, 132 lb from stall 21 makes life harder for a gelding rated just 61 officially.

runners_data.name: Navagio
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type who has faded in recent finishes and has a sim-going record of 0W 0P from 15 good-ground runs — wearing tongue-tie, style fit 0.92, and the age profile suggests this horse is operating below the level needed to make an impact.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Navagio at least returns quickly after running just eight days ago and has experience of today's trip and going, but a mark of 61 and a draw of 19 leave him with plenty to prove from mid-division.

runners_data.name: Wegotogether
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll rides this Gavin Cromwell four-year-old who won on good ground but in sprint distances — the pace hood is fitted and while the horse has ability, being a true hold-up type racing out of role (style fit 0.91) in a 21-runner field is a significant ask.|
runners_data.comment: Wegotogether won last time out, which is a genuine tick, but she ranks 17th of 21 on our figures and hails from a yard firing at just 3% in the last 14 days — hard to fancy at the weights from stall 18 despite having run over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: All Hail
runners_data.note: Ben Coen rides this A Oliver three-year-old who wears a hood and is flagged for fading in the finish — eight runs on good ground without a win, and a style fit of 0.92 confirms this horse is disadvantaged by not finding its natural back-of-the-field position.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, All Hail arrives on the back of an eighth last time out and has found little in recent outings, though he has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 20-day break looking for better luck from stall 13 carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Cladach
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old ran just yesterday (1 day since last run), which is an immediate red flag for freshness — a natural hold-up horse shuffled into midfield by the field dynamics (style fit 0.91), with Declan McDonogh unable to compensate for the positioning compromise.|
runners_data.comment: Cladach has run over today's trip and going, and his recent placings — second last time out and third two starts back — show he retains form, though he remains winless in his last six and ran just yesterday, making the quick turnaround a concern.

runners_data.name: Little Miss P
runners_data.note: Gillian Scott's four-year-old mare has been off 57 days and has 0W 1P from nine good-ground starts — a true hold-up horse operating out of her comfort zone in this large field, with a style fit of 0.92 reflecting the tactical difficulty.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with two unplaced efforts among them, Little Miss P ranks near the foot of our figures and faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip and going before, and a 57-day break at least means she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Expound
runners_data.note: Top-weight front-runner for Denis Hogan, a bold-going seven-year-old with tongue-tie and pace hood — the form of -54047 and sim-going record of 1W from 9 shows ability, but carrying 143lbs at the head of the market in a two-way pace duel with Star Strewn makes this a war of attrition from the front.|
runners_data.comment: Expound has run over today's trip and going but remains winless in his last five starts, with a pair of fourth-place finishes his best recent efforts; a struggling trainer and a speed rating of 68 ranked ninth of twenty-one make it hard to see him breaking through from stall two.

runners_data.name: Gloriously Glam
runners_data.note: Claire O'Connell's four-year-old prominent racer with the pace hood has two wins from 15 good-ground runs and placed 2nd at 8f recently — the prominent style is genuinely suited to this race shape and the horse has fitness on its side having run eight days ago.|
runners_data.comment: Gloriously Glam arrives here just eight days after her last outing, winless in her recent starts, though a second three starts back shows she can mix it with better; drawn at stall one and carrying 131 lb, her experience over today's trip and going helps, but the weight is a stern ask.

races.paceDynamic: Expound and Star Strewn are the two confirmed front-runners in a 21-runner mile handicap on good ground at Cork, and with both likely to want to lead, there will be a genuine early battle for supremacy that sets an honest, pressured gallop from the outset. Star Strewn has course form and is lightly weighted enough that Rory Cleary will be committed to the front, while Expound, a notoriously bold-going type carrying top weight, will not be easy to pass in the early stages — the result is a race run at a true clip throughout. The field holds considerably more hold-up and prominent types than can find their natural position; Storm Averted, All Hail, Elusive Duke, Wegotogether, Navajo Point, Navaijo, Cladach, and Little Miss P are all genuine hold-up horses who will be forced further forward than ideal in a 21-runner heat, compromising their ability to deliver a true late finish. With a genuinely contested pace burning up the front end of a flat mile on good ground, this race shape most strongly favours horses who can race prominently just off the pace — close enough to track the speed without being embroiled in the early duel — and then sustain their run into the straight when the leaders inevitably flatten out.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Trackers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Expound and Star Strewn go hard early and tie each other up, leaving the race to horses racing just behind at a comfortable tempo.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other out through the middle of the race on good ground over a flat mile, and the prominent horses who have tracked just off the pace without spending bullets early inherit a clear advantage in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Star Strewn — asserts early dominance and the other capitulates, allowing a controlled lead at a manageable tempo.
scenarios.body: With a solo lead established through the first half of the race, the pace becomes regulated and the leader is never truly challenged until late, making it difficult for hold-up horses to close the gap in time on a flat mile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the front-running duel is truly brutal and the pace collapses spectacularly, allowing horses from midfield to come with a powerful late run.
scenarios.body: Horses like Comfort Line, Highbury See See, and Blues Emperor, who are genuine hold-up types properly positioned, can produce a sustained finish if the race is run to suit their style from the front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If true hold-up types that have been mapped to midfield — Storm Averted, Elusive Duke, Wegotogether — manage to find cover and deliver their finish despite racing out of their natural role.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because those horses are compromised by the crowded field and their redistribution away from ideal positioning, but a messy pace or traffic benefits them marginally.

watchPoints.text: Expound and Star Strewn will clash for the lead immediately — watch the early splits, because if neither concedes, the pace could be unusually fierce for a flat mile handicap and both will be vulnerable entering the final two furlongs.

Cladach ran just one day ago — monitor for signs of staleness or injury in the pre-parade and early stages; a horse asked to race again within 48 hours in a 21-runner field is a significant welfare and form flag.

Elusive Duke (Colin Keane) and Wegotogether (Gary Carroll) are natural closers who will be forced to race closer than ideal — watch whether either jockey elects to drop out regardless and make up ground from an unfavoured position, which would signal confidence in the horse's ability.

Holy Lettuce and Sherekiya both carry unclassified tactical profiles (U) — watch their positioning in the first two furlongs to understand whether they track the pace or drop away, as their eventual race shape is genuinely unknown and could make them difficult to catch.

Gloriously Glam carries the pace hood and has a genuine prominent style in a field where most prominent slots are contested — if she secures a clean run in second or third position behind the duelling front-runners, her freshness (8 days) and recent placed form make her a horse to follow through the race.
